"Reality" is a structural-role term (§1.1): its reference is fixed not by pointing to an individual but by a role: *being what any real content belongs to*. Stage 2 showed what fills that role, in every world: T ∧ S ∧ Φ. That does not make this weld a wholly independent proof alongside maximality and exhaustion; it makes it the role-semantics version of the same identity.

::: {.argument}
**The Role-Semantics Weld** · *from structural-role co-reference to Reality being Nature*

1. "Reality" refers by structural role — what any real content belongs to and presupposes (§1.1).
1. "Nature" names the three Conditions (succession, distinction, exchange) under their positive description (§1.4).
1. *(Stage 2) Triconditional necessity.* That role is filled, necessarily and everywhere, by T ∧ S ∧ Φ.
1. A role-term and the name of the role's necessary filler co-refer in every world at which they refer at all (steps 1–3).
1. So "Reality" and "Nature" co-refer necessarily (□(R = N)), at the resolution Stage 2 supplies (step 3).

:::

*Dependency.* §1.1 (structural-role anchoring) + §1.4 + Stage 2. *Honest note:* this is structural-role co-reference, not the natural-kind rigidity of *water = H₂O*. As §1.1 makes explicit, "Reality" is not a natural-kind term in Kripke's typology but a structural-role term *continuous with* it; the necessity here is exactly as strong as the role-anchoring (no stronger), and the full natural-kind parallel is argued at §2.6 / §2.9.5, not assumed here.
